dedupe_keys.name: model data on the yield potential of offshore wind energy for the whole north sea with wake effects for build out years 2025 to 2050 bsh fraunhofer iwes

description: The Bundesamt für Seeschifffahrt und Hydrographie (BSH) publishes, with Fraunhofer IWES, model data on the energy yield of offshore wind farms across the whole North Sea, prepared for the German offshore area development plan (Flächenentwicklungsplan). Contents: hourly fields of wind speed and wind direction at nine heights between 50 m and 350 m, air density and the power output of the wind turbines in each grid cell, computed with the WRF numerical weather model and the Fitch wind farm parameterisation extended by Vollmer et al. (2024), so that wake losses between farms are included; series exist for a reference scenario and for build-out scenarios of the years 2025, 2030, 2035, 2040 and 2050, plus multi-year runs for single months of 2017 to 2021 in the German part. Coverage: the North Sea including the waters of all bordering states, at 2 km by 2 km resolution, for the meteorological year 2006. Format and access: files listed through GovData and the BSH GDI download feeds (gdi.bsh.de), with a description of the variables in the files. Licence: Datenlizenz Deutschland Namensnennung 2.0 (dl-by-de/2.0); free. Caveats: a single weather year, assumed future farm layouts and one wake parameterisation, so absolute yields depend on those assumptions. Simulation uses: offshore generation profiles for power system capacity planning, grid connection sizing and scenario studies of North Sea wind build-out. Related records: none yet for BSH offshore planning data.
